evidence.finding: Current failure log: candidate.py:130 (_log10_streaming warmup, SUB=16384) fails BiSheng ConvertLinalgIRToBinary with 'ub overflow, requires 2097152 bits while 1572864 bits available' for log10_-timing-11 (float32, 16777216 elements) and 'requires 2621440 bits while 1572864 bits available' for log10_-timing-3 (float16) and log10_-timing-7 (bfloat16); 60/66 supplemental cases pass, no valid performance obtained.

Prior accepted result belongs to old source sha256 d5ba772425b156c2f9377b8c07ceb338c5045024f81169042d76690645c5f049 (geo_mean 0.8067895931x), not to the current source f574e5e5; used only as background for which large-input cases matter, not as evidence about the current compile footprint or speed.

hypothesis: The 16384-element streaming half exceeds the UB budget for every large-input dtype in the current compiler: per loop iteration both loads, both fp32 conversions, both mask/address vectors and both stores stay live, so peak UB per basic block scales with the half width (2 MiB required for float32, 2.5 MiB for 2-byte dtypes versus 1572864 bits available). The earlier claim that two 16384 halves reuse the already-compiled pair-tile footprint was wrong.
change: In _make_streaming_entry only: choose the streaming half width from element size. float32 uses SUB=8192, the half width of the previously accepted streaming geometry; 2-byte dtypes try SUB=16384 and drop back to 8192 when the warmup compile rejects that footprint. Grid, tail tuple, launcher/stream entry and fallback closure keep their current construction; kernel math, masking, tails and all non-streaming paths are untouched.
expected: The three large timing cases stop failing at compile time (no ub overflow), live UB per block stays within 1572864 bits, and each loop iteration still covers one 2*SUB tile. No speedup is claimed; performance must be measured by the host run.
validation: Preflight the edited candidate, then the host runs full KGS plus both references and the supplemental suite; require 66/66 supplemental cases and read measured timings before any performance statement.
alternatives: One global SUB for all dtypes (the failed 16384 choice) versus a dtype-aware half width that keeps live UB inside the 1572864-bit budget.
